subject: FinWise load test coordination — k6/Locust details & IP allowlist
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sally Chen <sally.chen@finwise.com>, Eric Park <eric.park@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-12T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: FinWise load test coordination — k6/Locust details & IP allowlist

Hi Sally / Eric —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and next steps so we can get the customer-led load test scheduled: 

Summary of SLOs you mentioned on the call:
- Target latency: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms for 1-2 token responses; p95 <= 500ms for longer streaming responses.
- Throughput: target sustained 150 requests/sec during peak windows, with 300rps burst capacity for short spikes.
- Concurrency: expect up to 60 concurrent sessions (streaming enabled).
- Streaming: you require chunked responses for partial outputs; end-to-end latency for first byte is most important.

What we need from you so we can run the customer-led load test:
1) Test window(s) — preferred dates/times (please include timezone).
2) IP ranges to allowlist (we will coordinate with our infra).
3) Test accounts or test API keys (we can create scoped test keys that hit a sand-boxed model pool).
4) Load script(s) you plan to use (k6 or Locust). If you want, we can host a small starter k6 script and a Locustfile for you to iterate.

Attached: a short test plan and example scripts (k6 and Locust) to use as a baseline.

Next steps: if you can confirm test window and provide IP ranges, Rishi will provision test keys and a temporary dedicated pool for the run.

Thanks — I’ll loop back with a proposed runbook once we have the window.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: finwise-loadtest-plan.pdf (pdf)
From: Sally Chen <sally.chen@finwise.com>

Cc: Eric Park <eric.park@finwise.com>, FinWise SRE Team <sre@finwise.com>
Date: 2027-03-12T18:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinWise load test coordination — k6/Locust details & IP allowlist

Thanks Logan — great recap. Confirming the initial details from our side: 

- We can run two 2-hour windows next week: Tue 2027-03-16 09:00-11:00 PDT and Wed 2027-03-17 13:00-15:00 PDT. Prefer Tue first.
- IP allowlist: 52.43.12.0/24, 18.205.47.96/27 (our infra team provided these blocks).
- We will use k6 for the main ramp and have a Locust test ready for long-tail concurrency scenarios. I’ll attach the k6 script and Locustfile after internal review; for now please assume the following test profile:
  * Ramp: 0 -> 150 vus over 8 minutes
  * Sustain: 150 vus for 60 minutes (we will shorten to 20 minutes for first smoke)
  * Burst: short 5-minute window at 300 vus
  * Streaming tests: 50 concurrent streams to validate chunked responses

We will need a test key and an endpoint that preserves streaming semantics. Also want to validate p95 at the end of the 60-min sustain.

SRE will be on standby during the runs (Eric and team).

— Sally
Sally Chen
Director, Platform Engineering, FinWise
sally.chen@finwise.com

Looping in to coordinate infra config and test keys. Quick notes from our side: 
- We can provision a scoped test API key that routes to a dedicated pool (no production traffic). Key will be rate-limited to the requested test profile but will allow bursts up to 400rps for short durations.
- For streaming semantics we will provide a streaming-enabled endpoint (same base URL, different route) so your client can receive chunked output.
- Please confirm whether you need TLS client certs or just IP allowlist + API key.

I attached a brief runbook (finwise-loadtest-plan.pdf) and example scripts. Rishi — can you create the key + temp pool once Sally confirms the window and IP ranges?

Thanks — Marissa

I’ve attached the scripts and the locustfile. Let me know if you want us to run a control run from our side first.

— Rishi
